the desegregated classrooms of the 1970's and 1980's will produce more positive results if the classroom is designed to encourage cooperation in the pursuit of common goals.

interdependent structures in the desegregated elementary school classroom increase the self-esteem, morale, interpersonal attraction, and empathy of all students, and improve the academic performance of the disadvantaged students.
structured interdependence is a more effective method for achieving desegregative goals than is unstructured cooperation.

the question, "What happens when students are forced to work together in the pursuit of common goals?"

the development of a classroom climate which promotes the achievement of common goals through interdependence, and in which the individual's self-concept is not dependent upon the achievement of these goals.
the question: Can a desegregated school be a better place for students to learn and to grow?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the desegregated classrooms of the 1960s and 1970s have not produced the positive social and academic outcomes that were expected, largely because they have been based on an overemphasis on competitiveness and an underemphasis on interdependence.

interdependence is a viable alternative to the competitive model of education, and that it is an alternative that has the capacity to improve the academic and social climate of desegregated classrooms.
the desegregated school is an excellent place to begin, but it is not a sufficient place to end if the goal is the achievement of racial harmony.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
structured interdependence is an effective means of promoting the positive social, emotional, and academic effects of desegregation.
interdependent, cooperative, and collaborative learning structures can produce positive outcomes for all students in desegregated schools.
the desegregated, interdependent classroom can be a positive social experience for all students.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students can be taught to be cooperative and interdependent in the classroom.
the classroom should be a place where students are encouraged to work together in pursuit of common, interdependent goals.
the classroom should be viewed as a social system in which students must learn to interact with one another in pursuit of common academic and social goals.
